skilltree.name: diagram-construction
skilltree.description: diagram-construction: a diagram is a formalized relationship structure, never decoration — never begin by drawing; determine what exists, how it relates, what changes, what causes what, where the boundaries are, and what loops, and only then ask what it should look like; every visual primitive must possess an interpretable function

children.name: chainforge
children.description: a diagram is a formalized relationship structure, never decoration — never begin by drawing; determine what exists, how it relates, what changes, what causes what, where the boundaries are, and what loops, and only then ask what it should look like; every visual primitive must possess an interpretable function

children.name: diagram-construction-loop
children.description: the diagram-construction default workflow — walk it

children.name: entity-extraction-cor
children.description: a node represents a distinguishable unit and needs a reason to exist — type it and level it before it enters any graph

children.name: edge-typing-cor
children.description: an arrow is not generic association, proximity is not causality, a container is not ownership — every relation gets an explicit type and a real direction

children.name: boundary-abstraction-cor
children.description: a boundary defines inside, outside, interface, and crossing conditions — and abstraction layers stay stable across every chain

children.name: topology-selection-cor
children.description: the diagram type follows the system logic, never taste — relations or chronology, cycles or not, hierarchy or network, magnitude or membership

children.name: graph-validation-cor
children.description: an orphan node has no reason to exist, an ambiguous arrow is a lie, and invisible feedback is a hidden loop — find them and repair the graph

children.name: legibility-render-cor
children.description: topology before styling, color as category never decoration, and a viewer must be able to infer the intended reading order — density over budget splits into overview plus subsystems
